title: In my game, scrolling back up un-happens your death — so there's no restart button
author: Wilfred3D
selftext:
Scrollyo is played entirely with your scrollbar. No buttons, no keys, nothing to click. The only input is how fast you scroll.

A mote is caught in a current. Scroll fast and it sinks, scroll slowly and it rises. The current also braids sideways and reverses every \~400px of depth, so speeding up doesn't steer you — it just commits you harder to whichever way you are already leaning.

The part I'm happiest with: your scroll position *is* world time. So when you lose the mote, you scroll back up and it un-happens. There's no restart button because there's nothing to restart — you take the same passage again at a different speed. The game doesn't even call them deaths. It counts them as "retaken", and that's all it ever says about them.

Two ways in. A daily descent generated from the date, so everyone gets the same water that day — those runs are replayed on the server before they rank. And an endless one that never stops getting harder, which is the multiplayer one: up to ten people in the same water, and you can see where everyone is. Nobody can get in your way, ever. Other players are drawn and nothing more.

Free, no account, no install, and it works offline.

[**https://scrollyo.com**](https://scrollyo.com/)

I'd genuinely like to know how the no-restart thing lands. It's the whole design and I still can't tell whether it reads as generous or as taking the stakes out.
